verdict.rationale: Unity's own docs say the Editor accepts command-line arguments to 'automate workflows', and its Build Automation service runs CI multiplatform builds. A runtime probe notes the editor's -batchmode/-nographics CLI is documented for headless CI builds, but the pack has no first-party doc excerpt showing a scripted build/export invocation, so coverage is only partial. The community complaint about CI build servers concerns seat cost, not capability, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: first-party docs showing a headless editor build/export command (e.g. batchmode with a build target or build method), explicit evidence that self-hosted CI runners can produce exported player builds without the GUI, and independent hands-on corroboration of headless CI builds.

support.subject: As a game developer, I can build and export the project from the command line, headless, in CI — no human clicking an editor

citations.quote: You can launch the Unity Editor and Player with additional command line arguments to control startup behavior, configure settings, or automate workflows.
the entry point to the editor whose -batchmode/-nographics CLI is documented for headless CI builds
Use Unity Build Automation and its continuous integration features for multiplatform builds.
Build Automation supports most popular version control systems and builds for multiple platforms simultaneously, including iOS.
